summary: Customer reports three debit card purchases totaling $1,240 at an out-of-state retailer on a card they still hold.
Charged two $35 overdraft fees on the same day although a payroll deposit posted that morning.
Charged $389 for an airline ticket that was cancelled by the airline; merchant refund not received after 30 days.
Servicing transferred in August; payments sent to the prior servicer were not credited and a foreclosure notice was issued.
Collection agency calls the customer at work three times a week about a personal loan paid off in March.
A 30-day late payment was reported for May even though autopay records show the payment was made on time.
Online subscription charges of $14.99 per month for six months that the customer never signed up for.
A $2,500 Zelle payment went to a scammer posing as the bank's fraud department; customer asks for the money back.
Customer received a repossession notice while a payment deferral was being processed by phone.
An extra $400 principal payment was applied to future interest instead of principal.
Account frozen for a fraud review for 9 days; customer cannot pay rent.
Residual interest of $23 charged after the customer paid the statement balance in full.
Monthly payment rose $310 after an escrow analysis the customer believes double-counted the tax bill.
A credit card the customer never opened appears on their credit report with a $3,100 balance.
A $1,800 mobile check deposit has been on hold for 8 business days without explanation.
Customer is being collected on for a medical bill that insurance already paid.
